## Reading this file

This is a semantic architecture document. It describes the actual product,
runtime, data, security, emulator, native renderer, web player, operations,
tests, benchmarks and known limits. It intentionally contains no generated
index, filler, source dump, user records, ROM contents, session
cookies, secrets, environment-file values or SSH private keys.

When documents disagree, current source, tests, deployment scripts, and live
staging `/health` responses are authoritative. Older handoffs are retained as
historical context. Production is outside the scope of this artifact and was not
accessed, changed, restarted, or packaged for the 0.4.3 Phase 1 release.

## Executive status

AN3 Arcade (Ăn 3 Tô Cơm) is a bilingual Vietnamese/English browser game library
served by a small Python standard-library HTTP application with SQLite. Game
emulation is client-side: EmulatorJS/WASM and browser canvas execute on the
player device. The server stores metadata, ROM/media files, accounts, sessions,
analytics, upload staging and same-origin EmulatorJS assets; it does not emulate
games or render frames on the TV Box.

The current native work adds an EmulatorRust/Tauri macOS shell. GBA and NDS
software framebuffers follow software framebuffer → Vulkan → MoltenVK → Metal.
3DS/Azahar retains a native Vulkan image/semaphore path and avoids a frontend
GPU→CPU→GPU round trip. The native renderer uses reusable persistently mapped
upload slots, a bounded two-slot default ring, low-latency fences/semaphores and
error recovery that drains pending one-shot waits before replacing a frame.

The current web player exposes clean session/core/video/input/audio/save-state
boundaries. `?renderer=webgl2` selects the available WebGL2 canvas. `?renderer=webgpu`
is a safe test selector: the bundled EmulatorJS core still owns a WebGL canvas,
so the request falls back explicitly rather than pretending to be a WebGPU
implementation. A real worker/WebGPU/OffscreenCanvas/AudioWorklet migration is
deliberately deferred until a compatible upstream EmulatorJS runtime exists.

## Product and user journeys

### Public library

The home page is a bilingual library with search, system filters and per-system
sections (GB/GBC/GBA, NDS, 3DS, Doom and HTML5/custom where present). Games may
be visible in Draft, Testing or Release without login. A prepared library
fingerprint allows the browser to detect a changed catalog without polling while
hidden; the visible library refresh logic is bounded and does not reload the
page automatically.

Each game has a detail page with bilingual title/description, cover, system,
status, file size, screenshots, update history, rating summary, comments and
report/favorite actions. Recommended ordering prefers eligible GBA Release
entries before lower-confidence/testing entries. Files are delivered with
streaming and HTTP Range support.

### Accounts and community actions

Registration uses a fixed login name plus editable display nickname. Passwords
require the configured minimum length; new hashes use scrypt with a per-password
salt. PBKDF2 remains only for reading legacy hashes or as a fallback on Python
builds without scrypt. Sessions store a hashed token, CSRF token and expiry;
cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure on HTTPS production.

Authenticated users can rate a game once on a 1–5 scale and update that rating,
favorite/unfavorite, comment, and submit a categorized playback/control/other
report. Contributions have honeypots, duplicate suppression, account/IP quotas,
minimum spacing and bounded body lengths. Logout clears the server session.

### Administrator journey

Only an authenticated admin sees Dashboard and admin APIs. The dashboard covers
ROM/cover/screenshot upload, bilingual metadata, Draft/Testing/Release status,
game deletion, enrichment proposal review, report moderation, contact links,
admin creation, nickname editing, analytics and system metrics.

Large ROM uploads use a resumable 8 MiB chunk protocol when the direct request
would be too large for the proxy. Upload sessions have a TTL, offset checks and
safe temporary names. The filename/type classifier infers GBA/NDS/3DS and other
systems from extension, archive members and naming hints. ZIP files are inspected
without blindly extracting untrusted paths; NDS keeps the original ZIP for
melonDS, while browser-prepared paths are generated only where the core requires
them. Custom HTML5 games are sandboxed under `/custom/<game-id>/`.

Batch status changes are previewed, capped at 50 selected games and require a
typed confirmation. Enrichment remains pending until an explicit admin approval;
ROM bytes are not modified by enrichment.

### Player journey

The player exposes a stable toolbar for menu, save/import state, quick-save slots,
fullscreen, performance settings, speed (session-only), cast/TV discovery and
virtual-control visibility. The menu, virtual controls, NDS touch pad and
physical keyboard are layered around the EmulatorJS canvas so an input change
does not mix with save-state business logic.

On coarse/mobile pointers, the virtual pad is available for GB/GBA/NDS/3DS and
its layout, scale, opacity, visibility and orientation are stored per system.
Physical keyboard mappings and custom mappings remain available. NDS has a
separate dual-screen presentation and touch bridge; pointer/touch events are
mapped to the visible DS screen, canvas pointer capture is guarded, and the
native shell supports cursor lock with Esc releasing the cursor.

### Offline PWA journey

`/offline` is the supported offline surface. It stores local ROM handles/files
in browser-local storage (OPFS when available, IndexedDB metadata) and keeps the
EmulatorJS core contract in IndexedDB database `EmulatorJS-core`, store `core`.
The persistent core cache is `an3-arcade-cores-v1`; the readiness marker is
`an3-offline-core-v7:<channel>:<system>`. Offline data is device-local and does
not synchronize accounts, ratings, comments or the shared library.

The PWA can download and verify cores per system, recognize local ROM/ZIP files,
preserve the original NDS archive, launch with the same player toolbar/save
slots/fullscreen/touch controls, and remove indexed/cache entries through the
offline manager. HTTPS/PWA is required for durable Service Worker/Cache Storage;
plain HTTP LAN still supports IndexedDB but not a fully reloadable offline shell.

## System topology

The deployment topology is deliberately split:

1. A browser or installed PWA connects to public HTTPS through the Cloudflare
   tunnel or directly to the staging LAN endpoint.
2. The Python app serves HTML, static assets, ROM/media Range responses, APIs,
   `/health`, and same-origin EmulatorJS proxy paths.
3. SQLite and media live under an environment-specific data root. Production and
   staging have separate code roots, service units, cookies, databases, ROMs and
   protected environment files.
4. The browser downloads EmulatorJS/WASM assets through `/emulatorjs/<channel>/`
   same-origin paths backed by a checked server cache. Emulation, canvas and
   audio execute on the browser device.
5. The native macOS app embeds its own player shell and Rust/ObjC++ renderer;
   Azahar is hosted inside EmulatorRust rather than launched as an external app.

The staging unit is `an3-arcade-staging.service`, code root
`/opt/an3-arcade-staging/current`, data root `/srv/an3-arcade-staging`, and port
8092. The current staging release was switched only through the restricted
`an3-arcade-staging-release` wrapper, which preserves the previous symlink target
for rollback. No production release command was run for this artifact.

## Server implementation

`app.py` is a Python standard-library HTTP server with an explicit data-root
configuration. Major responsibilities are:

- static asset version hashing and pathname-versioned boot assets;
- environment-aware HTML pages and bilingual translation helpers;
- SQLite initialization, WAL mode and foreign-key enforcement;
- password/session/CSRF handling and rate limits;
- game inference, safe path resolution, archive inspection and prepared ROMs;
- public pages, player/preload pages, offline page and download-app page;
- admin APIs for uploads, metadata, status, enrichment, reports and metrics;
- streamed files with Range requests and cache/content-disposition headers;
- Service Worker rendering with the active asset version;
- health and bounded read-only host metrics.

The request dispatcher distinguishes public resources (static, EmulatorJS, cover,
screenshot, game file, health) from dynamic pages that need a session lookup.
This avoids a database session read for every CSS/core/ROM byte while retaining
account resolution for pages and mutations. API errors fail closed as JSON;
unknown browser pages become the localized 404 page.

### Main route groups

Public pages: `/`, `/login`, `/register`, `/account`, `/game/<slug>`,
`/play/<slug>`, `/offline`, `/download-app`, `/core-preload/<system>`.

Files/assets: `/static/<path>`, `/static/v/<asset>/<boot-file>`,
`/service-worker.js`, `/emulatorjs/<channel>/data/...`, `/cover/...`,
`/screenshot/...`, `/download/<slug>`, `/game-file/<slug>`, `/custom/...`.

Public/auth APIs include registration, login/logout, rating, comments, favorites,
reports and library-version discovery. Admin APIs cover game creation/update,
direct and chunked uploads, cover/screenshot handling, game deletion, batch
status preview/apply, enrichment proposal review, admin users, report status,
contact settings and system metrics. The exact implementation is the source of
truth in `Handler.do_POST`, `Handler.do_PUT`, `Handler.do_DELETE` and the page
builders in `app.py`.

### SQLite model

The schema includes users, sessions, games, ratings, comments, favorites,
reports, site_settings, page_views, play_events, game_screenshots,
game_updates, upload_sessions, game_enrichment_proposals and related proposal
image/state records. Foreign keys are enabled and writes use transactions. The
server keeps ROMs/covers/screenshots/custom-game data outside SQLite and stores
safe relative paths plus metadata in rows.

Do not hand-edit a live production database, copy production rows into staging,
or remove media independently of the app's deletion path. SQLite WAL files may
exist while the service is running; backup procedures use SQLite Online Backup
rather than a raw WAL copy.

## Browser player layering

`static/player-runtime.js` defines the stable AN3 boundary:

- `EmulatorCore`: reads the EmulatorJS game manager and exports/imports raw state
  bytes without wrapping or changing the core format.
- `VideoBackend`: probes WebGL2/WebGL and records the requested renderer,
  selected backend, availability and explicit WebGPU fallback reason.
- `VideoSource`: advertises `SoftwareFramebuffer` and `NativeGpuFrame` as the
  forward-compatible source categories while the current EmulatorJS adapter
  references its external core canvas.
- `InputRouter`: translates AN3 virtual-button actions to core input calls.
- `SaveStateManager`: narrow state byte export/import boundary.
- `QuickSaveManager`: IndexedDB database `an3-arcade-save-slots`, object store
  `states`, raw state Blob per slot and bounded slot reads/writes.
- `AudioPipeline`: reports core-owned audio scheduling; AN3 does not tie audio
  to `requestAnimationFrame`.
- `FramePacingMonitor`: bounded timing samples, core-frame deltas and long-task
  observations without claiming unavailable dropped-frame/audio telemetry.
- `EmulatorSession`: composes the boundaries and exposes a single player-facing
  session object.

`static/player.js` owns core preload/report validation, performance profiles,
fullscreen, EmulatorJS menu layering, NDS/3DS canvas protection, touch-to-mouse
bridges, cursor/pointer handling, TV discovery/casting, quick-save UI, speed
controls, virtual-pad geometry and keyboard/player event ordering. Settings keys
are versioned and migrations are bounded so an old pad layout does not corrupt a
new system's controls.

Web quick-save behavior currently has five browser-local slots for compatibility;
native EmulatorRust exposes four stable slots (1–4). Both store raw core state
bytes and intentionally preserve existing formats.

## Native EmulatorRust architecture

The native Tauri application is version 0.4.3. Rust owns application/session
coordination and FFI-safe state/menu calls; ObjC++ hosts the macOS AppKit/Vulkan
surface and integrates the core adapters. The Azahar host is internal to the
EmulatorRust process and receives native core frames rather than opening another
application window.

### GBA/NDS software path

1. A compatible libretro core is initialized with a software framebuffer ABI.
2. When supported, `RETRO_ENVIRONMENT_GET_CURRENT_SOFTWARE_FRAMEBUFFER` returns
   the current reusable mapped upload memory so the core can write directly into
   a free slot.
3. The slot records geometry/format/pitch and uses native RGB565/XRGB/1555
   upload paths. CPU format conversion and intermediate memcpy are fallbacks,
   not the default.
4. A persistent Vulkan image, command buffer, fence and semaphores upload the
   frame. Texture/buffer/pipeline creation is outside the successful frame hot
   path and is repeated only for geometry/format changes.
5. Vulkan is presented through MoltenVK to Metal on macOS.

### 3DS/Azahar native path

Azahar can submit a native Vulkan image with acquire/release semaphores. The
frontend keeps the image on the GPU and presents it without copying through CPU
software memory. Pending one-shot waits are tracked explicitly. On a failed
replacement/present/shutdown path, a persistent drain command buffer submits the
matching image ownership/layout barriers, waits on every pending semaphore with a
fence, records the fence and clears pending state. This prevents lost binary
semaphore ownership and stops the host after an unrecoverable renderer failure.

### Buffering and synchronization

`AN3_FRAME_RING_SIZE` allows a bounded two- or three-slot upload ring. Two slots
are the default because the measured three-slot ring had no material throughput
gain and a larger latency bound. Fences are waited only when a slot is reused;
CPU emulation can overlap GPU upload/presentation while the bounded ring prevents
the emulator from running arbitrarily far ahead. There is no per-frame
`vkQueueWaitIdle` or `vkDeviceWaitIdle` in the normal path. Device-idle behavior
is reserved for reconfiguration or rare signaled-but-unconsumed binary-semaphore
recovery.

Metrics expose direct writes, copied frames, converted frames, dropped frames,
slot waits and bounded upload/present percentile timings. They do not fabricate
CPU, memory or audio-underrun values when the harness cannot observe them.

## Web renderer/cache architecture

The preferred future architecture is Main Thread = UI/input, Emulator Worker =
WASM/core, Render Worker = OffscreenCanvas, AudioWorklet = audio, with a
SharedArrayBuffer framebuffer ring when `crossOriginIsolated` is available and a
safe non-SAB fallback otherwise. That split is not claimed as implemented in
0.4.3 because the bundled EmulatorJS owns its WASM, canvas and audio lifecycle.

The implemented boundary keeps UI/input/save-state concerns outside the canvas
adapter and exposes renderer selection for controlled testing. The WebGPU query
is intentionally honest: if a browser advertises `navigator.gpu`, AN3 still
does not bind it to a copied EmulatorJS canvas. The user receives a notice and
the bundled WebGL2/WebGL fallback continues. This avoids adding a second frame
copy or breaking core audio/input while waiting for a compatible upstream build.

Boot cache upgrades are protected by a pathname version. The current Service
Worker shell references `/static/v/6a70df830ac0/offline.js`,
`player-runtime.js` and `player.js`; the server accepts only the current
12-hex asset and gives it `public,max-age=31536000,immutable`. The worker itself
is rendered from a template with the active cache name, and old aliases return
404. Legacy generic static query paths remain available for other assets.

## Input, touch, fullscreen and state invariants

- Menu actions do not rewrite save-state bytes.
- Native raw quick-save slots 1–4 map directly to `retro_serialize`/
  `retro_unserialize` output.
- Web IndexedDB state records retain existing database/store names and five-slot
  behavior.
- Physical keyboard mapping is persisted separately from core state.
- Virtual controls are scoped by system/orientation and can be resized, faded,
  hidden or restored without reloading the emulator.
- NDS uses the melonDS path with auto-start and a dedicated dual-screen layout;
  no DeSmuME/manual-start regression is reintroduced.
- NDS touch dispatch maps pointer/touch coordinates to the canvas video viewport,
  protects against third-party pointer capture, and releases safely on cancel.
- Native NDS cursor lock is released by Esc so the user can recover the desktop
  pointer.
- Fullscreen keeps the AN3 toolbar/status scope and does not silently drop the
  control overlay.

## Security and privacy model

The app uses CSRF tokens, HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, Secure cookies on HTTPS,
password hashing, session expiry, rate limits and role checks. Uploads enforce
size, offset, filename/path and expiry constraints. Comments/reports have
honeypots, quotas and duplicate suppression. CSP, `nosniff`, Referrer Policy,
Permissions Policy, COOP/CORP and frame restrictions are sent according to page
type; player pages allow only the required EmulatorJS/CDN/worker sources.

Production and staging are isolated by code root, data root, database, media,
cookie namespace, environment marker and systemd unit. Staging deployment keeps
the previous release and has a rollback script. SSH operations use the owner-
installed verified identity with password authentication disabled; this document
intentionally contains no key material, password, token or protected env value.

Cloudflare WAF/rate limits and tunnel configuration are separate operational
controls; this summary does not claim a setting that was not directly verified.

  **4 passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- macOS ARM64 Tauri release build: passed.
- `codesign --verify --deep --strict`: passed.
- `hdiutil verify`: passed.
- Staging health, Service Worker substitution, current immutable alias, wrong
  alias rejection and both renderer preload routes: passed.

The direct-frame AppKit/mock-core harness ran for 4.000 seconds:

- 237 frames, 59.25 FPS;
- direct writes 237, copied 0, converted 0, dropped 0;
- raw state save/load both succeeded;
- upload p95/p99 195/208 microseconds;
- present p95/p99 305/325 microseconds.

Ring comparison:

| Ring | Frames/FPS | Dropped | Upload p95/p99 | Present p95/p99 | Decision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 2 slots | 478 / 59.72 | 0 | 188 / 198 µs | 310 / 334 µs | default |
| 3 slots | 478 / 59.72 | 0 | 185 / 203 µs | 303 / 326 µs | no material gain; larger latency bound |

Historical real-core hardware measurements at a capped target were GBA 59.72
FPS and NDS 59.87 FPS, both with zero drops, and 3DS/Azahar 58.47 FPS with no
software uploads. These support stable pacing and latency; they do not claim an
FPS increase. CPU usage, memory, audio underruns and independent `T_emulate`
were not available from the current harness. The tiny browser fixture is not a
real ROM and is not used as gameplay evidence.

## Historical delivery timeline

- Earlier handoffs established the client-side EmulatorJS architecture, melonDS
  auto-start, NDS touch bridge, IndexedDB core contract and staging-first release
  discipline.
- EmulatorRust 0.1.x established the native shell, menus, raw saves and input
  mapping.
- 0.2.x integrated Azahar into the native shell and retained native Vulkan.
- 0.3.x added native GBA/NDS software-framebuffer paths.
- 0.4.2 formalized the Phase 1 renderer/session boundaries and initial cache
  versioning.
- 0.4.3 hardened CoreVulkan pending-semaphore recovery, corrected localized
  native asset paths, versioned boot aliases for upgrade safety, rebuilt the
  macOS ARM64 DMG and deployed staging asset `6a70df830ac0`.

## Known limitations and next work

1. A real Emulator Worker/Render Worker/OffscreenCanvas/SAB/WebGPU/AudioWorklet
   split is pending a compatible EmulatorJS worker/WASM build.
2. Native visual click-through for menu/key-map/cursor capture was source,
   compile and harness validated; the local macOS GUI session was locked during
   this run, so real-ROM interactive soak was not claimed.
3. Real licensed GBA/NDS/3DS ROM gameplay, audio and long-run thermal testing
   must be repeated on an unlocked macOS host.
4. Add real-core CPU, memory, audio-underrun, `T_emulate`, `T_upload` and
   `T_present` telemetry before comparing optimization profiles.
5. Integrate a true WebGPU backend only when it can consume a core-owned worker
   frame safely without a per-frame CPU copy; retain WebGL2 fallback and test
   `crossOriginIsolated` and non-isolated paths separately.
6. Re-run Android regression harness before any future player/mobile release.
7. Keep all future releases staging-first; production still requires explicit
   owner approval and a verified rollback preflight.

## Safe operational checklist

Before changing runtime code: read `AGENTS.md`, inspect the latest Phase 1
handoff, run local tests/benchmarks, build the native app if relevant, package a
staging archive, release only through the restricted staging wrapper, check
`/health`, exercise representative routes, verify the artifact hash and record a
new handoff. Never print protected environment values or private keys. Never
point staging at production data. Never use the broad production deployment
script for a staging-only task.

For rollback, keep the active staging release path and previous release target,
switch the `current` symlink through the staging rollback procedure, restart
only the staging unit, and re-check the staging health marker. Database restore
is a separate, owner-approved operation and is not part of a normal code
rollback.
